::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
**Scientist at Eawag**, Swiss Federal Institute of Aquatic Science and Technology,
Dübendorf, Switzerland.
:::

I am a freshwater ecologist working on biodiversity, restoration ecology and ecosystem
function, with field-based research across wetlands, rivers, lakes, springs, intermittent
streams and ponds. My work combines ecological experimentation, biodiversity monitoring and
interdisciplinary approaches to understand how aquatic vegetation dynamics and restoration
interventions affect both ecosystems and the people who use them.

I did my MSc at ETH Zürich and my PhD at Université de Rennes 1, where I studied the impacts
of macrophyte management in an international, interdisciplinary setting. I then spent three
years at WasserCluster Lunz on the Horizon Europe project
[RESTORE4Cs](research.qmd#restore4cs), examining coastal wetland restoration as a tool for
climate mitigation. Alongside this I lead [EUPHORIA](research.qmd#euphoria), a Europe-wide
project coordinating more than 110 early-career researchers to study macrophyte phenology and
build citizen science around it.

I have worked in Switzerland, Germany, Austria, France, Lithuania, the Netherlands, Romania,
Spain, Portugal and South Africa.

## Current focus

- **Coastal wetland restoration and greenhouse gases** — leading meta-analyses on how
  restoration changes carbon storage, GHG emissions and biodiversity.
- **Macrophyte phenology across Europe** — coordinating EUPHORIA, a distributed
  early-career collaboration spanning 22 countries.
- **Early-career representation in aquatic science** — executive board member of the
  International Society of Limnology (SIL) as Global Outreach ECR representative.
